AfterObtained.rationale: PaelsEye.cs:58-62 sets only WasOwnerPartOfLastPlayerTurn, whose own doc comment (PaelsEye.cs:38-42) says it exists for the multiplayer case where two players hold Pael's Eye and one of them is force-ended without drawing. Waived as multiplayer-only under the shared contract's explicit exclusion, not under an unreachability claim about ported content: the field is initialised True (PaelsEye.cs:21) and the only writer other than this hook is AfterSideTurnStart, which in single-player always takes the `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` branch and re-assigns True (lines 96-100).

BeforeCardPlayed.rationale: PaelsEye.cs:64-84's entire body after its four guards is `base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal` (line 82) -- the relic-bar glow going out once you play a card. Presentation only; the sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation exclusion, the same verdict audit/records/relic/unsettling_lamp.json N5 and audit/records/relic/belt_buckle.json N1 give RelicStatus writes (binding rule 3).

AfterSideTurnStart.rationale: PaelsEye.cs:86-107 writes base.Status (presentation) and WasOwnerPartOfLastPlayerTurn (the multiplayer field waived on AfterObtained above). In single-player `participants` always contains the owner, so the branch taken is always lines 98-99 and the field is always re-set True -- the value the sim's absence is equivalent to.

ShouldTakeExtraTurn.maps_to: should_take_extra_turn (paels_eye.py:36-40), dispatched by HookSystem.should_take_extra_turn (hooks.py:662-671) from CombatState.end_turn (combat.py:648)
ShouldTakeExtraTurn.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and G3 per binding rule 4. The predicate itself maps clause for clause -- `!UsedThisCombat && !AnyCardsPlayedThisTurn() && WasOwnerPartOfLastPlayerTurn` (PaelsEye.cs:111) against `not self.used_this_combat and not self._any_cards_played_this_turn()` -- but the flag is never reset (G1), the played-cards test counts auto-plays C# excludes (G2), and the sim evaluates the whole thing at the WRONG POINT in the turn-end sequence (G3). C#'s `return player == base.Owner` (line 113) is structurally satisfied: hooks.py:669 passes the combat's single player.

BeforeSideTurnEndEarly.maps_to: folded into on_extra_turn (paels_eye.py:42-47), dispatched by HookSystem.on_extra_turn (hooks.py:673-680) from combat.py:649
BeforeSideTurnEndEarly.issue: MECHANISM: PaelsEye.cs:118-128 exhausts the hand from Hook.BeforeTurnEnd's SECOND sub-slot (Hook.cs:1250), i.e. inside the ordinary turn-end pass and BEFORE the extra turn has even been decided; its four guards (line 120) merely re-derive the same condition ShouldTakeExtraTurn uses. The sim moves the exhaust into on_extra_turn, which fires AFTER the decision and INSTEAD of the turn-end pass. The exhaust itself is faithful (`for card in list(player.hand): ExhaustCmd.exhaust(...)` mirrors `CardPile.GetCards(Owner, PileType.Hand).ToList()` + `CardCmd.Exhaust`), so this entry carries guard G3's verdict, not an independent one. See G3 for the executed evidence.

AfterTakingExtraTurn.rationale: PaelsEye.cs:130-140 does Flash() + base.Status (presentation, waived as N4) and `UsedThisCombat = true`. The sim sets the same flag. The `player != base.Owner` bail (line 132) is structurally satisfied by the single-player CombatState. NOTE the collapse per PROMPT.md bug class 15: the sim maps TWO C# hooks (BeforeSideTurnEndEarly and AfterTakingExtraTurn) onto one method, and their C# guard sets are NOT identical -- the exhaust checks four conditions, the flag-set checks only ownership. Because the sim only ever calls on_extra_turn when should_take_extra_turn already returned True, the union it applies equals the exhaust's set, and the flag can only be set on a turn the exhaust also ran. So the collapse is lossless HERE; what is not lossless is the timing, which is G3.

AfterCombatEnd.issue: PaelsEye.cs:142-147 is `base.Status = RelicStatus.Normal; UsedThisCombat = false;`. The sim clears used_this_combat nowhere. Carries guard G1's LIVE label; the Status half is presentation.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): `used_this_combat` is never reset, so the extra turn fires in the FIRST combat of a run only (PROMPT.md bug class 13)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: paels_eye.py:25 initialises the flag False in __init__ (which runs ONCE PER RUN, when RunState.add_relic constructs the relic) and paels_eye.py:47 sets it True; nothing ever clears it. C# clears it at PaelsEye.cs:145 AfterCombatEnd. Relic instances live on RunState.relics and are re-attached to every new CombatState (relics/base.py:152-154), so combat 2 enters should_take_extra_turn with the flag already True. FIRST READER traced per bug class 13: paels_eye.py:38's `not self.used_this_combat`, the very first clause of should_take_extra_turn -- nothing shadows it, because the relic has no combat-start hook at all. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py eye-reset`): combat 1 reports should_take_extra_turn=True, one end_turn spends it, and the SAME instance in combat 2 reports used_this_combat=True / should_take_extra_turn=False where a FRESH instance in the identical combat reports True. CONFIRMS .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep A, whose pool-wide sweep-reset-exec reached the same field (`self.used_this_combat: False -> True`) -- re-derived only far enough to add the observable, which the field diff does not show. Both sides ported: the relic comes from the ported Pael shrine and every run has more than one combat. Same one-line fix as relic/belt_buckle G2 and relic/centennial_puzzle: clear the flag in an on_combat_start.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): `AnyCardsPlayedThisTurn` -- C# excludes AUTO-plays and filters by actor (PaelsEye.cs:156); the sim counts every CardPlayedEntry (paels_eye.py:27-34)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# queries `History.CardPlaysFinished.Any(e => e.Actor == base.Owner.Creature && e.HappenedThisTurn(...) && !e.CardPlay.IsAutoPlay)`. The sim's history has no auto-play flag at all: combat.auto_play_card routes through the same _resolve_card_play bracket (combat.py:553 -> :514) that hooks.on_card_played fires from, and CombatHistory.on_card_played (history.py:80-81) appends an undifferentiated CardPlayedEntry. So an auto-play the player did not choose spends Pael's Eye's turn. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py eye-autoplay`): HellraiserPower auto-plays any Strike the moment it is DRAWN (powers.py:706-713), and the turn-start draw happens before the player can act, so a turn can contain auto-plays and zero manual plays. Probe output: 5 auto-played Strikes, `_any_cards_played_this_turn = True`, `should_take_extra_turn = False`, where C# gives False/True. Both sides ported -- Hellraiser is in the Ironclad card pool (cards/pool.py:26) and the starting deck is Strikes; MayhemPower (powers.py:3568-3583) reaches the same shape from the draw pile. The actor clause is separately satisfied: the sim's history only ever records the single player's plays.

guards.what: G3 (LIVE): the sim's extra-turn path SKIPS the entire turn-end pass -- Hook.BeforeTurnEnd, DoTurnEnd, the hand flush and Hook.AfterTurnEnd all fail to fire
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# decides the extra turn LAST. CombatManager's turn end runs Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1179 -- itself three sub-slots, BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly then BeforeSideTurnEndEarly then BeforeSideTurnEnd, Hook.cs:1232-1262), then DoTurnEnd's ethereal exhaust and turn-end-in-hand cards (:1191), then Hook.BeforeFlush (:1204), then FlushPlayerHand (:1296), then Hook.AfterTurnEnd (:1307); only afterwards does SwitchFromPlayerToEnemySide consult Hook.ShouldTakeExtraTurn (:1366) and fire Hook.AfterTakingExtraTurn (:1381). The sim asks FIRST (combat.py:648) and `return`s (combat.py:652), so on_player_turn_end (= Hook.BeforeTurnEnd, combat.py:654), _process_turn_end_cards (= DoTurnEnd, combat.py:658), the hand flush (combat.py:661-662) and after_player_turn_end (= Hook.AfterTurnEnd, combat.py:665) are ALL skipped on the turn that grants the extra turn. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py eye-turnend`): a sentinel listener registered on the combat records ['on_player_turn_end', 'on_hand_emptied', 'after_player_turn_end'] without the relic and ['NONE'] with it, on the same end_turn call. Both sides ported: Pael's Eye comes from the ported Pael shrine (events/pael.py OPTION_POOL_3 / Pael.cs:52-63) and the sim has 30+ on_player_turn_end listeners and a live after_player_turn_end listener in relic/parrying_shield (also in this batch), so a turn-end effect being silently dropped needs no further content. Nothing shadows it: the sim never runs those slots later, and the next thing it does is start a new turn. CONSEQUENCES worth naming, both with content already in the sim: (a) relic/parrying_shield's after_player_turn_end never fires on a Pael's Eye turn, so its 6 damage is lost; (b) relic/paels_tears' on_player_turn_end never fires, so had_leftover_energy is not refreshed before the extra turn's on_player_turn_started reads it. The exhaust ordering difference is a consequence of the same defect: C# exhausts the hand BEFORE DoTurnEnd, so ethereal and turn-end-in-hand cards see an empty hand; the sim exhausts and then skips DoTurnEnd, which reaches the same empty-hand outcome by accident. This is a defect in the sim's end_turn machinery (combat.py:644-652) rather than in paels_eye.py, but Pael's Eye is the only ported should_take_extra_turn listener (`grep -rn 'def should_take_extra_turn' sts2_rl/` returns relics/base.py's absence, hooks.py:662 and relics/paels_eye.py:36 only), so the observable belongs to this record. NOTE per binding rule 7: the rationale leans on sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/hooks.py, which this record does NOT hash.

guards.what: N1: the WhisperingEarring turn-1 special case (PaelsEye.cs:152-155) -- on turn 1, holding Whispering Earring makes AnyCardsPlayedThisTurn return true unconditionally; the sim has no such clause
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# short-circuits so Pael's Eye can never grant an extra turn on the first turn of a combat while Whispering Earring is held (the Earring auto-plays your hand for you, which would otherwise be free). The sim reaches the same answer INDIRECTLY and only sometimes: WhisperingEarring.on_player_turn_started plays cards through `combat.play_card` (relics/whispering_earring.py:43), whose plays ARE recorded in the history, so `_any_cards_played_this_turn()` is True whenever at least one card was affordable and playable. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the concrete missing piece is named): the two answers differ only when the Earring plays ZERO cards -- a turn-1 hand in which nothing is playable -- because C# still returns true and the sim returns false and grants the extra turn. That needs a hand of five unplayable cards on turn 1, which today requires a deck built almost entirely of Curses/Statuses; no ported content produces one, and the 18 ported Curses arrive one at a time. Porting any effect that fills the opening hand with unplayable cards (or an Ironclad relic/curse that makes the whole hand unplayable) makes it live. Recorded as a gap, not a waiver: 'no ported content reaches the differing branch' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). Both relics are Ancient and reachable in one run -- the Pael shrine repeats across acts (events/pael.py's AncientEvent base) and Whispering Earring is a different Ancient.

guards.what: N2: `if (!CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress) return;` on BeforeCardPlayed (PaelsEye.cs:66-69) and `cardPlay.IsAutoPlay` / `cardPlay.Card.Owner != base.Owner` (lines 74-81)
guards.rationale: All three gate a body that only writes base.Status, so they gate presentation. Waived with the hook itself; recorded separately because the IsAutoPlay clause here is the same distinction the sim cannot make at G2's site -- so the source is consistent about auto-plays not counting, and G2 is a real omission rather than an ambiguity in the source.

The sim's on_extra_turn/should_take_extra_turn are player-side hooks reached only from CombatState.end_turn on the player's own turn (combat.py:648-649), so the participation test is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only in effect, per the shared contract's exclusion.

RelicModel.Flash() and base.Status are presentation only (the relic card's glow and its greyed/active state in the relic bar); the sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, matching audit/records/relic/unsettling_lamp.json N5 (binding rule 3).
